sections.heading: Dialysis treatments we offer
paragraphs: Our Dialysis Unit offers a range of treatment options to meet different patient needs:

cards.title: Regular dialysis for kidney failure
paragraphs: Conventional haemodialysis is a standard treatment for kidney failure. It uses a dialysis machine to remove waste products and excess fluid from the blood. Patients usually receive treatment two to three times a week, depending on their condition and doctor's advice.

cards.title: Dialysis for critically ill patients
paragraphs: For patients who are seriously ill or receiving treatment in an intensive care unit, some forms of dialysis provide slower or continuous blood filtration.
items: Continuous Haemodialysis: A prolonged treatment that continuously filters waste and excess fluid from the blood. It is used for selected critically ill patients.
Slow Low-Efficiency Dialysis (SLED): A slower form of dialysis carried out over an extended period. It may be suitable for patients who cannot tolerate conventional haemodialysis.
Haemofiltration: A blood purification treatment that removes waste products and excess fluid through filtration.

cards.title: Other blood-cleaning treatments
items: Haemoperfusion: A treatment that passes blood through a special filter to remove certain toxins or poisons.
Plasmapheresis: A procedure that removes and replaces plasma, the liquid part of blood. It is used to treat certain immune-related and neurological conditions.

sections.heading: Your Care Team
paragraphs: Dialysis care involves more than the treatment itself. At IGCH, our nephrologist, Dr. Bibin Johny (MBBS, MD General Medicine, DM Nephrology), works alongside a team of dialysis nurses, renal dietitians and social workers. Together, they provide medical care, dietary guidance and practical support throughout your treatment.

sections.heading: Worried About the Cost of Dialysis?
paragraphs: The cost of treatment should not prevent anyone from seeking the care they need.
As a co-operative hospital, Indira Gandhi Co-operative Hospital in Kadavanthra, Kochi provides free dialysis sessions to eligible patients who need financial assistance.
Our team can explain the eligibility criteria and application process before treatment begins. Contact us to learn more about the available support.

faqs.question: What dialysis treatments are available at IGCH in Kochi?
answer: The Dialysis Unit offers conventional haemodialysis, continuous haemodialysis, SLED, haemofiltration, haemoperfusion and plasmapheresis. The appropriate treatment is decided by the nephrologist based on the patient's medical condition.

faqs.question: Who is eligible for free dialysis at Indira Gandhi Co-operative Hospital, Kadavanthra, Kochi?
answer: Free haemodialysis sessions are available to eligible patients who need financial assistance. The hospital team can explain the eligibility requirements, documents needed and application process.

faqs.question: When should I consult a kidney specialist in Kochi?
answer: Consult a nephrologist if you have persistent changes in urination, swelling in the legs or face, unexplained fatigue or abnormal kidney function test results. The specialist can assess your condition and advise whether further tests or treatment, including dialysis, are needed.
